pledged as collateral for loans (including non-housing loans), and an anticipated increase

in NPLs due to the impairment of borrowers' repayment capacity. BFI loan portfolios are

heavily exposed through loans to the real estate sector (20-30 percent of total loans) and

by the use of real estate as primary collateral (a further 50-60 percent of total loans). As of

mid-March 2015, 83 percent of the BFI's loan portfolio was secured by real estate

collateral. Rises in NPLs are especially expected in the tourism, and, to a lesser extent, in

the manufacturing sector. In addition, BFIs have exposure to many small and medium sized
